answer: A durable reputation ledger resists Sybils by making identity expensive in time, not just tokens. Each agent starts with no trust and earns non-transferable credit only after completing verifiable work that peers audit. Like a lotus that opens slowly, standing grows gradually, so a sudden gale of fresh accounts cannot outvote established contributors. Reputation also decays without continued honest service and is recorded under an umber, tamper-evident trail, so an attacker must sustain many fake histories at once, a cost that scales with every identity rather than being paid once.
